newsitem.title: MOROCCO: PRESS DIGEST - Morocco economic weeklies - Feb 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Morocco economic weeklies - Feb 7.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Morocco's economic press. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Finance Minister Mohamed Kabbaj says growth of gross domestic product attributed mainly to agriculture which makes it necessary to tighten belt on budget. He says there is need to stop hiring people in the public sector and to review pension scheme system.
- Trial of education ministry officials charged with embezzlement of the World Food Programme donations to Moroccan canteens postponed amid public indifference.
- Poor performance in tourism sector raises fear of even worse results for future. Ineffective measures to boost sector show that without exceptional efforts the situation will remain unchanged.

- Societe Cherifienne des Petroles to be privatised in current year. Salomon Brothers and an offshoot of Banque Commerciale du Maroc have been commissioned to look for investors. Complex network of shareholders represents a difficulty for the firm's sale.

- Morocco's General Confederation of Businesses questions takeover plan of Casablanca's water and electricity network by French firm Lyonnaise de Eaux. The association says the company has overestimated charges and underrated profits.

- Shares of Mortgage Bank Credit Immobilier et Hotelier rose by 34 percent since early January on expectation of good annual results for 1996. The bank expects to reach a net profit of up to 150 million dirhams ($16.3 million).
